The two discussed regional and international matters and security coordination, according to Saudi state media. The visit was framed by Paris as a show of solidarity after Yemen's Houthis stepped up attacks on Saudi territory this month. Saudi Arabia has also agreed to supply France with additional diesel for as long as needed, while the UAE and Bahrain have pledged further monthly volumes. France and the UK are also sending defensive military assets to help protect Saudi Arabia, including the Red Sea port of Yanbu.

auto-235c5f9037d2.headline: El Salvador launches rescue mission for personnel seized by gangs in Haiti
auto-235c5f9037d2.summary:
El Salvador's president, Nayib Bukele, says his government has started a military operation to free four air force personnel who have been missing in Haiti since Sunday. The men were serving with the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force and were ambushed in Croix-des-Bouquets, an area held by armed groups, while returning from buying food. No gang has claimed the attack. Bukele warned that a much harsher response would follow if the men were not returned alive, while the mission's helicopters have struggled to reach them due to fighting.

The kidnapping comes as Haiti's gangs reportedly expand their reach and retaliate against civilians, and as the country's elections, due in December, were postponed indefinitely.

auto-4f169eb698dd.headline: Israel's vote may swap its leader but keep hard line on Iran
auto-4f169eb698dd.summary: Regional policymakers and analysts expect Israel's coming election to change who leads the country without changing its core approach. Iran would stay the main adversary, military force would remain the favored instrument, and Palestinian statehood would stay a distant goal. The analysts argue the 2023 Hamas attacks and the subsequent wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran have hardened these assumptions. They suggest a win for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, backed by far-right partners, could push Israel toward a tougher security stance, including escalation with Iran, tighter control of the occupied West Bank and a sidelined diplomacy.

Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and intelligence chief Hassan Rashad met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Riyadh, delivering a written message from Sisi to King Salman. auto-aa503153fab6.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov visited Tehran and met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, following earlier meetings between Pezeshkian and Vladimir Putin. The piece argues Russia has strengths for the role: nuclear expertise, a Bushehr power project, and a recently warmer relationship with Tehran. It also notes Russia has reasons to want a settlement, including its North-South transport corridor and ties with Gulf states. Whether the effort succeeds is not yet clear.

auto-1697f4a91808.headline: El Salvador launches rescue operation for technicians kidnapped by Haitian gangs
auto-1697f4a91808.summary:
El Salvador's president, Nayib Bukele, said his government has started a military operation to free four Salvadoran aviation technicians seized by gangs in Haiti. The men have been missing since an attack on their armoured vehicle in Croix-des-Bouquets, on the edge of Port-au-Prince, on Sunday. Bukele warned the gangs that a much harsher response would follow unless the men are released alive, while stressing that El Salvador's mission in Haiti is non-combat. Haiti's government called the case an absolute priority, though it was unclear whether the men were confirmed alive.

The incident is the first major attack on the international gang suppression force since it began work in Haiti, where gangs are said to control about 70 percent of the capital. El Salvador is one of several contributors to the force, which has more than 2,000 troops deployed.

auto-c10b56443417.headline: Iran reports seven tankers hit in Hormuz amid renewed war fears
auto-c10b56443417.summary: Iran's state broadcaster said seven oil tankers were struck by attacks or hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz overnight on October 22, 2026. Four were reportedly caught fire while transferring oil, and three were disabled after striking mines. If confirmed, it would be the largest single-day count of damaged vessels in the waterway since the Iran war began on February 28. The Revolutionary Guard's navy warned that any U.S. effort to move tankers through what it called illegal passages could widen its retaliation to American bases in the region.

Officials say no scheduled outage timetable is in effect for these areas yet, and scheduled cuts will only be set once the grid stabilises. Ukraine's energy ministry says repair crews are being slowed by the attacks, repeated air-raid alerts and the risk of further strikes. The overnight attack on 21-22 October reportedly involved missiles and 210 drones, with Kyiv as the main target; air defences said they destroyed 181 drones. Residents are being directed to local grid operators for updates.

The request follows a visit by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to Egypt in mid-September, after a truce in Yemen collapsed that month. Five people linked to the firm, a ship management company running seven Panama-flagged vessels, and shipping agents in Singapore and the UAE were also targeted. The measures come as indirect US-Iran talks, mediated by Qatar and Pakistan, continue amid a stalled peace effort, with Iran keeping the Strait of Hormuz closed and the US maintaining a naval blockade.

Public transport has stopped after an attack on buses in neighbouring Kramatorsk killed 30 people. Of the city's roughly 100,000 residents, about 20,000 remain, mostly elderly people unable to leave. auto-c24a50c990ad.summary:

The Saudi Energy Ministry said the drone was aimed at the plant, and the debris started a fire in a contractor's vehicle outside the perimeter without affecting operations. The dead were Filipino and Nepali nationals; the injured were Pakistani and Indian. Saudi Arabia has faced a series of Houthi drone and missile attacks on airports, oil facilities and shipping, and the US State Department ordered non-emergency staff and families to leave the kingdom.

Separately, a Saudi strike on boats off al-Kadha in Yemen's Taiz Governorate reportedly killed eight fishermen, according to the Houthi-run health ministry, which called it a violation of humanitarian law. Earlier, a Houthi attack on King Fahd airport in Dammam killed one person and injured eight, Saudi civil aviation said.

auto-8f117f2c15a4.summary:

auto-b1643e8fdc4e.headline: Canada and Turkey elevate ties to strategic partnership in Ankara
auto-b1643e8fdc4e.summary:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan upgraded bilateral relations to a strategic partnership during Carney's first official visit to Turkey, held in Ankara. The framework covers trade, defence, energy and diplomatic cooperation, with a three-year action plan. Ministers also signed deals on energy, defence and air transport, and the two sides set a goal of lifting trade from about $3 billion toward $10 billion. Free trade talks are due to begin in Ankara next month. The move is seen as part of Carney's effort to diversify Canada's trade away from the United States.

Analysts quoted in the report said the visit signals to Washington that Ottawa is not waiting on it, while noting that Turkey's crackdown on the opposition and arrests of LGBTQ+ people have drawn criticism from rights groups.

Turkey gains investment and collaboration for its defence industry, nuclear plants and mining sector.

auto-50fe0e261bca.headline: Analysis: Russia and Ukraine positioned for decisive phase in Donbas fighting
auto-50fe0e261bca.summary:
An analysis piece from the Kyiv Independent examines the ground war in Donetsk Oblast, which has received less international attention even as fighting remains intense. Ukraine has had a comparatively successful 2026 on the front, with Russian net territorial gains largely flat and two Ukrainian counterattacks described as strategically significant. Russia's main aim remains taking the rest of Donetsk Oblast, and it has advanced toward the so-called fortress belt of cities including Sloviansk, Kramatorsk, Druzhkivka and Kostiantynivka.

The piece describes Russian drone range expanding over the area, making Ukrainian logistics harder and pushing civilians out. Russian forces overran much of Kostiantynivka in May and June, and pressure continues on Lyman in the north and Dobropillia in the south, as both sides seek the upper hand before winter.

Pressing for remaining Donetsk despite heavy casualties and flat territorial gains
Trump administration pressure on Kyiv shapes the political stakes of the front

impact_points: Ukraine faces a harder fight to hold Donetsk Oblast, with logistics strained and civilians leaving the fortress belt cities.
Russia continues pushing for the rest of Donetsk Oblast, a key condition in its demands for ceasefire talks.

auto-d5a46a9b9cea.headline: Seoul offers military talks with Pyongyang to ease border tensions
auto-d5a46a9b9cea.summary: South Korea has invited North Korea to military talks aimed at calming rising friction along their fortified border. Seoul's defence officials said the discussions could confirm the exact position of the land demarcation line, restore military communication channels and prevent accidental clashes. They suggested dates and venues could be set at Panmunjom and said they would welcome three-way talks including the US-led UN Command. It is unclear whether Pyongyang will accept, and North Korea has recently reinforced its border units and fortifications while rejecting earlier overtures and blame over a landmine blast that injured South Korean soldiers.

actors.why: Seeks to reduce border risks but faces a rejected earlier proposal
Has rejected talks and is reinforcing its border positions

impact_points: South Korea faces a growing risk of accidental clashes along the border if communication lines stay closed.

auto-9dbb196454ef.headline: Putin calls for talks centred on post-war security for Russia and Ukraine
auto-9dbb196454ef.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin told US envoy Steve Witkoff that any negotiations should focus on building a security framework for Russia and Ukraine once the conflict ends, according to Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov. Witkoff met Putin in St Petersburg a day after meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo. Ushakov said a new round could take place around 10 November in Abu Dhabi. Meanwhile, Kyiv was hit by a fresh missile attack that injured six people, and Zelensky said he would accept a ceasefire freezing the current front line.

European allies dispute Putin's claims and criticised US sanctions relief on Russia

auto-607f345088a4.headline: Kyiv struck again as Moscow signals readiness for renewed peace talks
auto-607f345088a4.summary:
Missile strikes hit Kyiv in several waves, hours after Russia said it was willing in principle to resume peace talks with the United States and Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky blamed Russia for the attacks, and a retail park in the city was reported destroyed. The strikes came shortly after US envoy Steve Witkoff described Russian President Vladimir Putin as a humanitarian following a meeting in St Petersburg.

The contrast between the diplomatic signal and the renewed bombardment sharpens doubts about whether talks can move forward. The report relies on footage and on-the-ground reporting from the damaged site.

auto-6b0b4f11f857.headline: Ukraine's General Staff claims Russia has lost over 1.57 million troops
auto-6b0b4f11f857.summary: Ukraine's General Staff reported that Russia has lost 1,574,620 troops since the full-scale invasion began on February 24, 2022, including 1,830 in the past day. The military also listed heavy equipment losses, among them thousands of tanks, armored vehicles and artillery systems. Ukraine does not publish its own losses, citing operational secrecy. Western think-tank CSIS estimates Russian casualties run roughly two to one, or two and a half to one, above Ukraine's. Those figures could not be independently verified.

auto-5254ac8cf3b1.headline: Two Palestinian suspects killed by Israeli troops after West Bank shooting
auto-5254ac8cf3b1.summary:
Israeli forces shot dead two suspected Palestinian attackers near the Judea Junction area, close to Hebron, on Friday, according to the Israeli military. An early-morning shooting had wounded at least five people, two of them in critical condition, Israel's emergency medical service said. The Israeli military said searches in the area were continuing.

The incident comes amid rising tension in the West Bank, including violence by Israeli settlers against Palestinian olive harvesters, and just days before Israeli elections. Separately, foreign ministers from Europe and the Middle East were meeting in Istanbul to discuss the Strait of Hormuz, Yemen, the Palestinians and the Russia-Ukraine war.

auto-bfbd5ef1f724.headline: EU enters winter with record-low gas stocks, IEA chief warns of price risks
auto-bfbd5ef1f724.summary: Fatih Birol, head of the International Energy Agency, has warned that Europe is entering winter with gas reserves far below historical norms, leaving it exposed to further supply shocks. Speaking in Berlin, he said disruption through the Strait of Hormuz linked to the US-Israel war on Iran has pushed up liquefied natural gas costs, and a harsh winter could drive prices higher. EU storage stood at about 72 percent of capacity against a usual 90 percent, and EU energy ministers are reportedly considering rationing.

Attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz have disrupted global energy flows
Ukraine's attacks on refineries cut Russian diesel deliveries, though Russia's gas leverage in Europe persists

impact_points: The European Union faces higher gas and diesel costs and possible rationing for households and industry this winter.

auto-4ff6ae5a7d4b.summary: EU leaders plan to press the UK, Canada and Japan to contribute more money to Ukraine's defence and civilian needs in 2027. Brussels says these G7 partners have not responded to earlier requests for extra aid, and Ukraine faces a reported funding shortfall of about 70 billion euros. The European Commission president will raise the matter with Canada's prime minister in Toronto, and with the UK prime minister at an EU-UK summit in Brussels on 20 November. The same summit is expected to address post-Brexit issues such as food standards, emissions trading and youth mobility. UK figures cited by the Kiel Institute put British support at a lower share of GDP than some Nordic and Baltic states.

auto-afaa4c8d3ed2.summary:

The talks covered regional issues and security coordination. The trip came as Houthi attacks on Saudi territory have intensified, and France described it as a show of solidarity with the kingdom.

Alongside the visit, Saudi Arabia agreed to supply additional diesel to France for as long as needed, and the UAE and Bahrain also made monthly supply commitments. France is also deploying military assets to help protect the Red Sea port of Yanbu, and the UK plans to send fighter jets. Both countries describe their support as purely defensive.

The site is traditionally linked to Eleazar the Priest, a figure important in Judaism and the Samaritan faith. Troops said the suspects fled before soldiers arrived, and police and forensic teams planned to enter the village under military escort. A regional council head condemned the act and visited the site for repairs. auto-0f92ee51fc89.summary: A magnitude-7 earthquake struck the northern Tibet region of China late on Thursday, according to official media. At least 16 people died and 54 were injured, and hundreds of homes collapsed in the city of Nagqu, with rescue teams working through the ruins. The epicentre lay about 191 km east-northeast of Nagqu in a sparsely populated, high-altitude area, and the US Geological Survey recorded at least seven aftershocks. auto-93b65002a809.headline: Sarawak's assembly to dissolve, setting up a state election that tests Anwar

The ruling GPS coalition, which has become important to Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's federal government, is seeking more autonomy and control over the state's oil and gas wealth. A new building with casting pits is at least twice the size of the existing one, which they say points to larger solid-fuel missiles with greater range or payload. auto-bebc523784d1.headline: Romania accuses Russia after drone sinks cargo ship off Black Sea coast
auto-bebc523784d1.summary:
A cargo ship, the Khoryv, sank after a drone strike about 24 km off Romania's Constanta port, which Romanian and European officials blame on Russia. One crew member died and three are missing, with nine rescued, according to Romania's naval authority. The vessel was flagged in Comoros, carried Ukrainian and Azeri sailors, and was heading for the Sulina port on the Danube. Romania's president and prime minister condemned the attack, and NATO said it would send more patrol aircraft, radar and drones to the Black Sea. Russia had not publicly responded at the time of reporting.

auto-a9fe9a6d53a1.summary: India's embassy in Yemen said on Friday that all 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht caught up in an incident off Yemen's coast appear to be safe and are located near Hodeidah. auto-f22c00f68160.summary: European Union trade ministers have said they intend to address a surge of Chinese manufactured goods flooding European markets by engaging directly with Beijing. auto-c41bbcbe0c61.headline: Attacks on shipping near Hormuz reach a record monthly high
auto-c41bbcbe0c61.summary: Data from a Washington-based think tank shows October was the most intense month yet for attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waters. The institute counted 28 attacks in October and 113 since the conflict involving the US, Israel and Iran began on February 28. The International Maritime Organization's figures broadly match, listing more than 30 damaged supertankers, 11 of them in October, roughly 3.5% of the global very large crude carrier fleet. Analysts said Iran may be stepping up attacks to slow the recovery in shipments and keep pressure on energy markets before the US midterm elections in November. The UK maritime security service said under-reporting by shippers means the full picture is hard to capture.

auto-b2c211964991.headline: France readies 70,000 police for weekend protests amid fears of unrest
auto-b2c211964991.summary:
France will send around 70,000 police across the country this Saturday as it prepares for fresh demonstrations. The move follows some of the most serious urban violence seen in years, which broke out on the fringes of protests a week earlier. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez announced the deployment at a Paris press conference and said social media posts were calling for violence and looting. President Emmanuel Macron convened his defence council and was reportedly postponing a late-month trip to Nigeria and Senegal because of the crisis.

The unrest grew out of school students' protests over conditions in their schools and has widened into a nationwide expression of anger at the government over the rising cost of living. Macron was also due to meet representatives of high school pupils for the first time.

auto-110f3bda7e51.headline: Electronics still reach Iran via smuggling, but fees and sanctions push prices up
auto-110f3bda7e51.summary: Electronics such as new iPhones, laptops and game consoles are still on sale in Tehran despite Apple having no presence in Iran and a US naval blockade of Iran's southern ports. auto-db54c6535b38.summary: An oil slick from a tanker damaged near the Strait of Hormuz has spread along the United Arab Emirates coastline, prompting closures of some beaches and coastal areas. auto-5e04699f8847.headline: UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh joins race for next UN Secretary-General

The UAE's Minister of State Lana Nusseibeh has entered the contest to succeed António Guterres as UN Secretary-General, challenging Costa Rica's former Vice President Rebeca Grynspan, who narrowly led an informal Security Council straw poll. The race has been relaunched after two opposing votes, allowing new candidates to join. A winner needs at least nine Security Council votes and no veto from the five permanent members, with a decision targeted by the end of December before General Assembly confirmation.

Nusseibeh, 48, a former UAE ambassador to the UN, pitches herself on peace, security, development, human rights and reform. Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it struck several tankers, a claim Washington disputes. Global emergency oil stocks, already drawn down heavily since the conflict began in February, are now at their lowest in decades. Analysts estimate that only about 400 million barrels of usable reserves remain outside China, and that a full closure of Hormuz and Houthi blockades at Bab al-Mandeb could cut Middle Eastern exports sharply.

auto-2ef7fc79ba84.summary: The US Embassy in Ottawa has accused Canadian ministers and provincial premiers of trying to influence the November US midterm elections, pointing to meetings with Democrats and calls for retaliatory tariffs. auto-2e631e566e93.summary: The US State Department has ordered non-emergency government staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, citing escalating hostilities with Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis. Saudi authorities reported three deaths from strikes across the kingdom, including two from drone debris near an oil field and one at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, where eight others were hurt. auto-78c6610038f0.headline: Iran reportedly plans to target Gulf undersea internet cables in any renewed war
auto-78c6610038f0.summary:

They gave few specifics and did not say where or how attacks would occur, though one said Iran would try to block repairs to prolong outages. Iran's Revolutionary Guards deputy political chief, Yadollah Javani, separately said seven major cables under the Strait of Hormuz could be targeted. The US State Department and Iran's Foreign Ministry did not respond, and Gulf states had no immediate comment.

Analysts quoted in the piece said the global effect could be limited, since less than 1% of international bandwidth passes through the strait, though multiple cuts could still slow internet services and disrupt finance and cloud computing.

auto-722f01f1fd49.headline: UN says Houthi blockade of Yemen's Taiz is cutting off aid and water
auto-722f01f1fd49.summary: The United Nations has warned that time is running out to deliver aid to Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, after Houthi fighters encircled it in early October. The group has blocked the road linking the city to Aden, the interim seat of Yemen's internationally recognised government. UN humanitarian agency OCHA said fighting has made it impossible for aid to enter and for people to leave, and called for safe, sustained access. Speaking in Geneva, spokesman Jens Laerke said road closures and diesel shortages had halved the city's water production and roughly tripled the cost of trucked water that most residents rely on.

Saudi Arabia is linked to the Yemeni government's position and regional stability

The internationally recognised government in Aden is cut off from one of Yemen's largest cities, complicating its authority there.

auto-22e17825a33d.headline: Analysts see signs of possible renewed US strikes on Iran
auto-22e17825a33d.summary: Analysts say the United States may be preparing to resume large-scale strikes on Iran, though neither side appears to have a clear military path to victory. Both sides have so far traded attacks on commercial shipping, with the US enforcing a blockade of Iranian ports and Iran pressing control over the Strait of Hormuz. Experts point to troop and asset movements, travel warnings and Israeli alert levels as possible indicators, and note that the war is unpopular in the United States because of higher fuel prices. Timing remains uncertain, and analysts suggest a diplomatic or military resolution will be needed.

Costly blockade, unpopular war and fuel price pressure before midterms
Israeli forces on high alert and jointly engaged in the war
Houthi allies of Iran may be drawn into expected strikes

auto-c84d555f9335.headline: Gunman kills one and wounds five in drive-by shootings west of Paris
auto-c84d555f9335.summary: A gunman fired from his car at people across the Paris suburbs of Trappes and La Verrière on Friday, killing one person and wounding five others, three of them seriously. The rampage lasted roughly 15 minutes and included attacks at a petrol station, a medical centre and a playground. A 12-year-old girl is among the injured. French interior minister Laurent Nuñez said the attack was clearly terrorist, and the national anti-terror prosecutor's office is investigating it as murder linked to a terrorist enterprise. A 39-year-old suspect has been arrested; his motive remains unclear.

impact_points: France faces a violent attack on civilians near Paris, prompting a terrorism investigation and heightened security concerns.

auto-1689e56d8786.summary: Turkey's foreign minister, Hakan Fidan, warned in Istanbul that any renewed attack on Iran would deepen tensions and spread the conflict further, insisting diplomacy is the only path to ending it. He hosted counterparts from Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Germany, France, Britain and Italy, the first joint meeting of that group, to discuss the Iran war, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Russia's war in Ukraine. The discussion followed a report that US and Israeli militaries had drawn up plans for strikes on Iranian energy, nuclear and missile sites after the November midterms. Possible parameters to prevent wider escalation were discussed, though no details were given.

Under Houthi attacks and seeking regional support against them

Warns renewed escalation would only bring losers and higher oil prices

auto-9785630b1e4e.summary: A gunman firing from a vehicle in a Paris suburb on Friday killed one person and wounded several others, including a 12-year-old girl. French authorities are treating the attack as possibly racially motivated. A suspect has since been arrested. The reporting describes the incident as a shooting from a moving car in a town on the outskirts of the French capital.

impact_points: France faces another violent incident in the Paris region, raising security concerns for residents and authorities.

auto-89df6503e6e8.headline: US lists helium as critical material amid chip supply strains
auto-89df6503e6e8.summary:
The United States has formally classified helium as a critical material, pointing to its central role in chip production and energy work. The US Department of Energy says the designation opens up extra federal funding for helium producers and tighter government oversight of supply. The decision comes as conflict in the Middle East and export restrictions from Russia and China tighten global availability. Helium exports from Qatar have been hit by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz and by strikes on Qatari infrastructure, while Russia imposed temporary export limits in April. Europe, which has struggled to secure supply, also faces a temporary Chinese export ban imposed in July.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright framed the move as part of a push to lessen reliance on foreign sources and expand domestic manufacturing. Europe has been affected through reported Russian helium reaching the continent via China despite an EU import ban on Russian helium from 2024.

Helium exports disrupted by Hormuz closure and strikes on its infrastructure

Europe faces tighter helium availability, with supply strained by the Chinese export ban and Middle East disruptions affecting its share.

auto-bdc70320d65a.headline: First Russian diesel cargo sails for New York under eased US sanctions
auto-bdc70320d65a.summary: A tanker carrying about 40,000 tonnes of ultra-low sulphur diesel loaded at Russia's Baltic port of Primorsk and is heading toward New York, with arrival expected around 7 November, according to the shipping data firm Kpler. The cargo would be the first Russian diesel shipment to the United States tracked by Kpler since July 2023. It follows an early October arrangement announced by President Trump that temporarily eased US sanctions on Russian diesel, while Russia lifted its own export ban. The move is widely seen as an effort to bring down fuel prices before the US midterm elections, and it has drawn criticism from Ukraine and its allies. The buyer and seller have not been publicly identified.

auto-1bb10375dd7f.headline: Melania Trump-brokered localised truce to open Oleshky for aid and evacuations
auto-1bb10375dd7f.summary: The White House says Melania Trump helped secure a temporary ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine around Oleshky, a Russian-occupied city cut off from food, medicine and clean water. Both governments confirmed the deal, which is set to start on 29 October, to allow aid deliveries and evacuations. The statement did not give an end date for the truce. Residents trapped between the front lines have reportedly been eating garden weeds to survive.

Russia must allow aid and evacuations in its occupied city, under pressure over shortages.
The US first lady brokered the deal, boosting Washington's diplomatic role.

Ukraine and Russia both gain a humanitarian channel, and the US position as broker is enhanced, though the truce's duration remains unclear.

auto-30f8097ee934.headline: Russia, Ukraine and US to resume talks in Abu Dhabi in November
auto-30f8097ee934.summary:
The Kremlin says trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States are planned for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, the UAE. Spokesman Dmitry Peskov announced the round, which follows a meeting between US envoy Steve Witkoff and Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg. Earlier US-brokered rounds this year made little progress, and Zelenskyy warned that the outcome would depend heavily on Moscow. Moscow still presses demands including Ukrainian territorial concessions and no NATO membership.

The article also reports a White House claim of a localised ceasefire in Oleshky brokered by Melania Trump, and a 270-for-270 prisoner exchange announced by Russia's defence ministry. Ukraine's prosecutor general put civilian deaths since 2022 at more than 19,000.

The Kremlin says trilateral negotiations between Russia, Ukraine and the United States will take place in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. Expectations of major progress are low, as Moscow still presses demands including territorial handover and no NATO membership for Ukraine.

auto-1677c96907e1.headline: Collins wins tariff exemptions for Maine farm goods from US levies on Canada
auto-1677c96907e1.summary: Maine Senator Susan Collins, a Republican facing a close re-election race, said nine agricultural products important to her state, including blueberries, potatoes, apples and seaweed, will be exempted from American tariffs on Canadian imports. She argued that Maine farmers depend on equipment and materials from Canada that US suppliers cannot readily replace, and said she would keep pressing the administration for further relief and a broader trade deal with Canada. The move follows a trade dispute in which Canada retaliated against US tariffs, and Maine's economy, which relies heavily on Canadian trade, has been hit hard.

actors.why: Trade war with US continues; partial relief but broader deal still uncertain

auto-42f7485bc7dc.headline: Taiwan warns Chinese militia boats are probing its east coast and western Pacific
auto-42f7485bc7dc.summary: Taiwan's Coast Guard says China is pairing militia vessels with coast guard ships and a research vessel to expand what it calls battlefield preparation around Taiwan and into the western Pacific. It described a suspected militia fishing boat, Minfudingyu 07902, coming within about 2.7 nautical miles of Taiwan's restricted waters on August 16, and said it had dispatched a patrol boat to drive it away. The coast guard linked the activity to overlapping economic zones with Japan and the Philippines, which began maritime boundary talks, and said such grey-zone operations also pressure those two countries. Beijing has not ruled out force over Taiwan, and China says its operations there are lawful; these claims could not be independently verified.

auto-e7809c711b7e.summary: A senior member of Tigray's newly installed, federally backed interim administration has told rebel fighters to surrender their weapons and return home. The appeal followed a statement from a rebel army commander, Lieutenant General Fisseha Kidanu, vowing to keep resisting government-aligned forces after the Tigrayan People's Liberation Front lost control of the regional capital, Mekelle, in early October. Residents reported a drone strike in Mekelle that killed four people, though those casualties could not be independently confirmed. The fighting has effectively undermined the 2022 Pretoria peace agreement that ended the 2020-2022 war.

auto-37f37d6e1f0c.summary: Ukraine's Defence Ministry is still logging service disruptions to Starlink and Starshield terminals on the front line, according to sources cited by Ukrainska Pravda. Serhii Beskrestnov, a presidential adviser and radio technology expert, also reported no sign of lifting, saying occasional terminals exceeding the limit were more likely caused by SpaceX's algorithm or operating conditions.

auto-b50a0d05f0f6.headline: How long global oil reserves could last if US-Iran fighting resumes
auto-b50a0d05f0f6.summary:

Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed to have hit several tankers, a claim Washington rejected. Global emergency oil stocks, drawn heavily since the war began in February, are at their lowest levels in decades. Analysts say usable reserves outside China and the Gulf are limited, and that Hormuz closure combined with Houthi action in the Red Sea could cut Middle Eastern exports sharply.

Analysts estimate roughly 400 million barrels of usable stocks remain worldwide, with nearly half in Japan. China holds more reserves, while India's cover only about eight days of imports.

India's reserves cover only about eight days of imports, leaving it highly exposed to any supply disruption.

auto-3e6244f71864.summary: Foreign ministers from eight countries met in Istanbul to press for restraint after Washington signalled that another strike on Iran was possible. Israel's military has started demolishing buildings in the Hebron neighbourhood the gunmen came from, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has promised extensive action in the territory. auto-4951639d9af7.headline: Iran war costs weigh on US midterm campaigns in Michigan and beyond
auto-4951639d9af7.summary: Ahead of the US midterm elections, Democrats and some Republicans are campaigning against the cost of living, which they link to the US-Israel war on Iran that began on February 28. auto-9787df2e6c49.headline: Melania Trump-brokered local truce to aid Russian-held Oleshky
auto-9787df2e6c49.summary: A localised ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine is set to start on 29 October in Oleshky, a city Russia seized in early 2022. The White House said US First Lady Melania Trump helped secure the arrangement, which aims to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and let residents evacuate to Russia or Ukraine. Both governments confirmed the deal, with fire to halt at 02:00 GMT on 27 October, though the statement gave no duration. Residents have reportedly been living under blockade, short of food, medicine and clean water.

actors.why: Russian forces hold the city and agreed to the truce amid criticism of supply failures.
Kyiv gains a route to reach trapped residents and deliver aid to them.
Washington claims a diplomatic win through the First Lady's role in the deal.

impact_points: Oleshky residents, cut off by fighting and blockade, may gain aid access and evacuation routes.
Russia and Ukraine both face pressure over the humanitarian crisis, while the US highlights its diplomatic role.

auto-86342a948924.headline: US Embassy accuses Canadian officials of meddling in midterm elections
auto-86342a948924.summary:
The US Embassy in Ottawa has accused Canadian ministers and premiers of seeking to sway American politics ahead of the November midterm elections. In a fact sheet, it cited remarks and actions, including meetings with US Democrats and calls for retaliatory tariffs on states that back the current administration. Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ontario Premier Doug Ford rejected the claims, with Carney pointing to US trade measures as the origin of the dispute. Carney also announced a roughly C$9bn aid package in response to US tariffs.

The row adds to strained relations between the two neighbours, whose trade disputes have hardened under the second Trump administration. US Ambassador Pete Hoekstra has said Washington is watching Canadian politicians closely, and a petition seeking his removal has gathered over 280,000 signatures.

actors.why: Accused of interference and facing tariffs, but announcing a major aid package for workers
Embassy accuses Canada of meddling, and its tariffs drive the dispute

impact_points: Canada faces accusations of election interference that its leaders reject, adding strain to bilateral relations with Washington.
Canadian workers and companies are receiving aid worth about C$9bn while tariff disputes with the United States continue.

auto-a17002eff7e1.headline: Russia and Ukraine agree local ceasefire and plan peace talks for next month
auto-a17002eff7e1.summary:
Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a ceasefire in a contested town and to hold peace talks next month, according to the report. The agreement came as the parties signalled willingness to resume negotiations. The report also says Kyiv was struck again by missiles hours after the announcement, which Ukraine's president attributed to Moscow. Russia reportedly said it was ready in principle to resume talks with the United States and Ukraine.

The report also mentions a US envoy who met Russia's president in St Petersburg and described him in favourable terms. Details of the ceasefire's terms and its duration are not clear from the available text.

actors.why: Kyiv hit by missiles despite ceasefire agreement and talks plans
Agreed to ceasefire and ready to resume peace talks
Envoy met Putin, helping restart negotiations with Russia

impact_points: Ukraine faces continued missile strikes on Kyiv even as ceasefire and talks are announced.
Russia and the United States are positioned to resume negotiations, with the US envoy engaging directly with Moscow.

auto-e5e70a71dc3d.headline: US midterm voters link Iran war to rising fuel and grocery costs
auto-e5e70a71dc3d.summary: Democrats in Michigan are pressing their opposition to the US-Israel war on Iran as voters grow frustrated with higher petrol, diesel and grocery prices. Since the conflict began on February 28, Iran has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, pushing energy prices up. The average US petrol price has risen from under $3 to over $4.27 a gallon, according to the American Automobile Association. A recent Institute for Global Affairs survey found 60 percent of potential voters disapprove of Trump's handling of the war, while Republicans still largely back him.

actors.why: Rising energy prices and voter discontent over the war threaten Republican midterm prospects.
The conflict and disruption of Strait of Hormuz energy flows target Iran, which faces ongoing military pressure.
Israel is a direct party to the joint attacks on Iran that began the war.

impact_points: The United States faces domestic pressure on costs, with voters blaming the Iran war for higher living expenses ahead of the midterms.
Republican candidates are distancing themselves from the war, while Trump has hinted at renewed fighting after the vote.

auto-2d3d3a796e32.headline: Eight nations meet in Istanbul on Hormuz, Yemen and Ukraine
auto-2d3d3a796e32.summary:
Foreign ministers from eight European and Middle Eastern states gathered in Istanbul on Friday in a new format. Britain, France, Germany and Italy joined Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt. Their agenda covered reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which has been blocked during the Iran war, along with Yemen and efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine conflict. France's foreign minister warned that renewed escalation between Iran and the United States would hurt energy prices, and the group agreed to keep meeting regularly. Attacks by Houthi forces from Yemen on Saudi Arabia were also a central concern.

Turkey, which hosted the talks, is expanding its regional role, including through a defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia that Egypt has not yet joined. France and Britain have also pledged military support to Saudi Arabia against the Houthi threat.

actors.why: Under Houthi attack, with allied support secured but exports threatened
Targeted by calls for restraint and dialogue over Hormuz
Hosted talks and gained regional diplomatic profile
Pushing diplomacy and pledging forces to protect Saudi oil terminal
Deploying fighter jets to Saudi Arabia, facing energy price pressure
Declined to join the Mecca pact and refuses attacks on Yemen

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces Houthi attacks that have closed its main airport and threatened oil exports.
Europe and global energy markets face higher prices while the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked.

auto-30b1d9cba9be.headline: Rubio urges Cubans to act as Trump floats naval pressure on Havana
auto-30b1d9cba9be.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called on Cubans seeking political change to act now, a day after President Donald Trump told a rally in south Florida that US warships returning from the Iran conflict could intervene near Cuba. Rubio's social media post referred to a partnership with the CIA, which he framed as a route to change, though the wording was not clarified. Trump has raised the idea of military action against Cuba before, and the administration has recently announced criminal charges against former leader Raúl Castro. Rubio said talks with Havana had failed to produce a diplomatic path, and new sanctions followed.

actors.why: Faces renewed US military threats, new sanctions and calls for internal change
Pursuing pressure on Havana, though talks have stalled and midterm concerns persist

impact_points: Cuba faces renewed threats of US military action, adding pressure to an already severe economic and energy crisis.
Cuban residents seeking change are urged by Washington to act, while the Cuban government faces more US sanctions.

auto-74d529705229.headline: Saudi coalition says it downed Houthi missiles over Riyadh and Khamis Mushait
auto-74d529705229.summary: Saudi Arabia's coalition in Yemen said it intercepted and destroyed two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh and Khamis Mushait, along with two drones heading toward the southern region. The coalition's spokesperson, Major General Turki Al-Malki, also rejected Houthi claims that Riyadh had threatened tribal and civilian gatherings, calling them baseless and an effort to mislead the public and drag Yemeni tribes into the conflict. The report notes a later announcement of further interceptions, including missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu, and a meeting between the Saudi and Pakistani foreign ministers on regional developments, particularly Yemen.

actors.why: Targeted by Houthi missiles and drones; coalition intercepted them
Houthi militia launching attacks; tribes at risk of being drawn into conflict
Foreign minister met Saudi counterpart on regional security and Yemen

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces renewed Houthi missile and drone attacks on its cities and southern region.
Yemeni tribes are caught between Houthi claims and Saudi denials, risking being drawn into the conflict.

auto-8accb4afe4f5.headline: Israel imposes West Bank lockdown after deadly Hebron shooting
auto-8accb4afe4f5.summary: Israel has placed the occupied West Bank under a lockdown following a shooting near Hebron that killed two Israeli soldiers. Israeli forces carried out raids on Palestinian homes and detained residents during the operation. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned of a military campaign on a scale not seen since 1967.

actors.why: Residents face lockdown, raids and arrests across the West Bank.
Two soldiers killed; government escalating with a large military operation threatened.

impact_points: Palestinians in the West Bank face movement restrictions, home raids and arrests under the lockdown.
Israel faces heightened security tensions and the prospect of a major military escalation in the territory.

auto-cf5e13d26d33.headline: Pentagon labels China-funded campus cultural centres a national security threat
auto-cf5e13d26d33.summary: The US Department of Defense has added Chinese-funded cultural centres on American university campuses, known as Confucius Institutes, to its list of threats to national security. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced the move in a video posted on social media on Friday. He claimed the centres operate under different names and charters while pursuing the same goal of stealing intellectual property and influencing students. Hegseth also said the department had dismantled every such organisation over the past two months. The Chinese embassy in Washington had not responded to a request for comment at the time of publication.

actors.why: Chinese-funded centres labelled security threats and reportedly dismantled by the Pentagon
Pentagon moves to counter alleged Chinese influence and intellectual property theft

impact_points: China faces US restrictions on its cultural and educational outreach, with its funded centres now classed as security threats.
US universities hosting these centres may face pressure to close them, affecting students and academic partnerships.

auto-e051504517f7.headline: Kremlin confirms Oleshky truce and says evacuation timing is being coordinated with Kyiv
auto-e051504517f7.summary: Russia's Kremlin has confirmed a ceasefire around the town of Oleshky in Ukraine and says it is working with Ukrainian authorities on when civilians can be evacuated from the area. The statement signals that Moscow sees the local arrangement as a practical humanitarian step, though the article's details on timing and conditions are limited. The report focuses on Russian confirmation rather than independent verification of how the truce is holding on the ground.

actors.why: Kremlin confirmed the truce and frames itself as cooperating on evacuations
Civilians may be evacuated, but coordination with Russia carries political implications

impact_points: Ukrainian civilians in Oleshky could gain a safer route out if the evacuation timing is agreed.
Russia gains a humanitarian talking point, while Ukraine must coordinate evacuation details with Moscow.

auto-ed16abdcd0c5.headline: Iran reports record tanker attacks in Hormuz as US escorts and warnings escalate
auto-ed16abdcd0c5.summary:
Iran says seven oil tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz in a single day, the worst toll for the waterway since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran in February. The Revolutionary Guards claim four ships were struck while transferring oil and three were disabled by mines, though these claims could not be independently verified. The IRGC also threatened US bases across the region if Washington helps vessels transit the strait.

US Central Command rejected the mine claims, saying the shipping lanes have been cleared and 95 percent of vessels are passing through. President Trump accused Tehran of inflating attacks to push up oil prices before the midterm elections.

Faces Iranian threats to its regional bases and rising fuel costs
Named as a party to the war that began on February 28
Port of Muscat shown as a shipping hub near the strait

impact_points: Iran faces a US blockade and rising attacks on shipping while it claims control over the strait.
US tankers, oil markets and American voters face higher fuel costs and pressure to avoid a wider war.

auto-a25ab8ed2c9d.headline: Kremlin confirms Oleshky truce and coordinates evacuation timing with Kyiv
auto-a25ab8ed2c9d.summary: Russia's government has confirmed a ceasefire covering the Oleshky area in Ukraine and says it is working with Kyiv on when civilians can be evacuated. The Kremlin's announcement addresses a local humanitarian arrangement rather than a broader settlement. The article's details on the terms and the timetable are limited in the material available, so specifics beyond the confirmed truce and the evacuation coordination cannot be verified here.

actors.why: Kremlin confirms truce and leads evacuation coordination with Kyiv
Oleshky civilians may be evacuated under the ceasefire, Kyiv's coordination needed

impact_points: Civilians in and around Oleshky could be moved out under a temporary halt in fighting, if the evacuation goes ahead.
Ukraine and Russia are both tied to the timing, so any delay or dispute over the schedule would affect both governments.

auto-4350dbea4f6d.headline: Israel imposes West Bank lockdown after deadly Hebron attack on soldiers
auto-4350dbea4f6d.summary: Israel has placed the occupied West Bank under a lockdown following a shooting near Hebron that killed two Israeli soldiers. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has warned of a military operation of a scale not seen since 1967.

auto-4ddaa686a3c2.headline: Drone-assisted evacuation of a wounded Ukrainian soldier from Kharkiv front
auto-4ddaa686a3c2.summary: Ukrainian commanders say they carried out what they believe is the first aerial drone evacuation of a wounded soldier from the front line. Kostiantyn Vlasenko, 49, had been stranded for months in the Kharkiv region after a Russian drone strike killed his comrade and injured him, costing him both feet's use. Commanders first tried unmanned ground vehicles, but drones destroyed two of them. A heavy-lift drone then lifted him about 15 kilometers to safety in early October, and he is now in rehabilitation in Kharkiv. The account comes from Vlasenko and the reporting does not independently verify every detail.

actors.why: Shows a new rescue method for wounded troops under heavy drone threat
Russian drones struck the position, but the evacuation hit nearby Russian drone operators

impact_points: Ukraine's armed forces gain a new method for extracting casualties where drones make ground movement deadly.
Russian drone units face a clear example of Ukrainian counter-measures and strikes on their nearby positions.

auto-1a1d242ba0d6.headline: Gunmen kill seven at church funeral in Jordan's Karak
auto-1a1d242ba0d6.summary: Seven people were killed and at least 34 wounded when gunmen opened fire on a church in Hmoud, in Jordan's Karak governorate, during a funeral. The attackers reportedly arrived by car, entered the grounds and fled after the shooting. No group has claimed responsibility. Jordan's interior minister called the perpetrators an extremist group and said authorities were pursuing them. The death toll was first given as six before being revised to seven. Lebanon's president condemned the attack, which the report describes as rare in Jordan.

actors.why: Deadly church attack; security and community trust under strain
Lebanon's president condemned the attack as violating religious values

impact_points: Jordan's Christian community in Karak faces a deadly attack on a place of worship and mourners.
Jordan's authorities face pressure to catch the attackers and stop further violence against minorities.

auto-7ed7b7274203.headline: Ukraine and Russia swap 270 prisoners each in third stage
auto-7ed7b7274203.summary: Ukraine and Russia each exchanged 270 prisoners of war on Friday, the third stage of a swap process that began on August 19. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv received 261 military personnel and nine civilians, many of them defenders from Mariupol and other front-line regions, some reportedly convicted in Russia. Russia's defence ministry confirmed the exchange and said its returned personnel were in Belarus. The deal was brokered by the United States in May and is expected to total about 2,000 prisoners. Kyiv also thanked the US and the United Arab Emirates for securing the release of an English teacher, Stephen Hubbard.

impact_points: Ukraine gains back hundreds of its servicemen and civilians, including people long held since 2022.

auto-000de1374090.headline: Europe alarmed as Trump's warmer stance toward Putin unsettles Kyiv
auto-000de1374090.summary: Ukraine and its European partners are increasingly worried that Washington is leaning toward Moscow in the war. Recent moves cited include a diesel deal with Russia, steps toward easing sanctions, and a reported proposal for a summit between Trump, Putin and Xi Jinping. Kyiv has also faced Starlink restrictions and delayed US weapons deliveries, which fuel suspicions of US pressure on Ukraine. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas publicly accused American negotiators of trying to push Ukraine into surrender. Officials say European governments have rejected ideas linked to US envoys such as frozen Russian assets and resumed gas supplies.

auto-2a3701638da8.headline: Argentina names dozens of people killed during its military dictatorship
auto-2a3701638da8.summary: Forensic anthropologists in Argentina have identified the remains of at least 38 people who were forcibly disappeared during the country's last military dictatorship. The identifications were highlighted in a report filed near La Perla, a former clandestine detention centre that operated during that period. The findings add to decades of efforts to account for victims of the so-called Dirty War, when security forces held and killed opponents in secret. The article is a domestic human rights story with no direct international dimension.

actors.why: Domestic forensic progress on past abuses; families gain answers and closure

impact_points: Families of the 38 identified victims gain answers about relatives who were disappeared under the dictatorship.
Argentina's ongoing accountability work for past state abuses is reinforced by these forensic identifications.

auto-b359cc4e4510.headline: Israeli election campaign grows nasty with AI-generated attacks and personal smears
auto-b359cc4e4510.summary: Days before Israel's close-fought election, campaigns have become increasingly harsh, with candidates and activists using AI-generated images to paint rivals as weak, untrustworthy or dangerous. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc and that of centre-right challenger Gadi Eisenkot are reported to be roughly level in polls. Clips have included an AI depiction of Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei and a Hamas figure, and critics say Netanyahu's camp is stoking fear of Arab-Israeli parties. Some candidates who lost relatives in the post-October 7 wars have also faced personal attacks, and relatives of former hostages have been drawn into the rhetoric.

Iran's supreme leader is depicted in campaign AI content threatening Netanyahu over the conflict.
Campaign rhetoric linking Netanyahu's rivals to Palestine and Gaza fuels tensions affecting Palestinians.

impact_points: Israel faces a tense vote where the campaign's inflammatory tone may deepen divisions among its voters.
Arab-Israeli parties are targeted by campaign messaging that critics say portrays them as illegitimate coalition partners.

auto-538dd9a2d103.headline: Russia and Ukraine agree local ceasefire and plan peace talks next month
auto-538dd9a2d103.summary: Russia and Ukraine have agreed a ceasefire in a contested town and will hold peace talks next month, according to the report. The announcement came as Kyiv was struck again by missile attacks hours after Moscow signalled it was ready to resume negotiations. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky blamed Russia for the strikes, which hit a retail park. US envoy Steve Witkoff had met Russian President Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg earlier that day and afterwards described him in favourable terms. Russia said it was ready in principle to resume talks with the United States and Ukraine.

Agreed ceasefire and readiness to resume talks with US and Ukraine
Envoy's meeting with Putin revives US-led mediation efforts

auto-26f6a7ef08aa.headline: Injured Australian MP's condition upgraded to serious but stable
auto-26f6a7ef08aa.summary: Helen Haines, an independent Australian federal MP, has moved from critical to serious but stable condition, according to the Alfred Hospital in Melbourne. The 65-year-old lost both legs after authorities said she was deliberately struck by a car outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, north-east Victoria, on Monday. The alleged driver, 43-year-old Brendan Nugent, was arrested at the scene and has faced court on three charges, with police saying more could follow. Investigators have not yet established a motive and are examining whether drugs or medication were involved.

actors.why: Domestic attack on an MP prompts concern over political tone and security

impact_points: Haines and her family face a long recovery after losing both legs in the attack.
Australia's political community is reacting to the incident, with the Prime Minister calling for less shouting and more discourse.

auto-38d1b647ef5a.headline: Eight foreign ministers urge restraint as US weighs fresh strikes on Iran
auto-38d1b647ef5a.summary:
Foreign ministers from eight countries met in Istanbul to press Washington against new attacks on Iran and to call for renewed passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said none of the participants backed another military operation, arguing diplomacy was the only route to ending the conflict. The warnings came as the US ambassador to Turkiye, Tom Barrack, said a strike could happen that weekend, while saying the aim would not be regime change. The group also discussed Gaza, fighting in Yemen and the Russia-Ukraine war.

The R4 group of Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt separately condemned Houthi escalation and Israel's actions in Palestine, and urged an end to the Iran war through dialogue.

auto-a88feca510cf.headline: Kyiv residents endure nightly shelter life as Russian strikes intensify in 2026
auto-a88feca510cf.summary: Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, is facing a sharp rise in Russian attacks, with residents increasingly living under threat. Many families spend nights in subway stations, which double as makeshift shelters because there are too few protected spaces for the city's roughly four million people. The article describes a September drone strike that killed a 14-year-old boy in Pechersk and an October strike on a school in southwestern Kyiv, when pupils were already sheltering. Local military authorities reported 140 deaths in the capital in the first eight months of 2026, versus 172 across all of 2025. Attacks on energy and transport have also caused blackouts and shortages, raising concern about winter supplies.

auto-57745e9d4409.headline: Oil slick from struck tanker spreads along UAE coast, beaches closed
auto-57745e9d4409.summary:
An oil slick from a tanker damaged near the Strait of Hormuz has spread along the United Arab Emirates coastline, leading to the closure of some beaches and coastal areas. The vessel, identified by BBC Verify as the crude tanker Gem No.2, was hit on 9 October during a surge of ship attacks in the region, which Iran is reported to have carried out. Satellite imagery indicates the slick had moved more than 35 km from the ship by Wednesday. UAE authorities say containment efforts have begun, while researchers say the full environmental damage is still too early to assess.

The spill is moving toward Siniyah and Khor Al Beidah islands, a recognised biodiversity area home to corals, seagrasses and endangered species such as green turtles and Halavi guitarfish.

auto-b9b9e2e26158.summary: A US envoy, Tom Barrack, said on Friday that Washington could carry out a strike on Iran as early as the coming weekend. He made the remarks in an interview, pointing to recent threats from both the United States and Israel. Barrack also said President Trump remains open to a negotiated agreement and that talks have been ongoing for months. The statement comes amid escalating rhetoric between the parties.

impact_points: Iran faces the prospect of military strikes while diplomatic talks with Washington remain unresolved.

auto-48630234e60a.headline: Iran's foreign minister claims US spent $11bn defending Israel from missiles
auto-48630234e60a.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi has claimed that the United States spent $11 billion of taxpayer money over three years on missile defence for Israel. Posting on X late on a Friday, he also said American forces have fired more interceptors in Israel's defence than Israel itself has. The figures were made by Iranian officials and reported by Mehr News from Tehran; they were not independently verified in this report. Araghchi described the bilateral relationship as parasitic rather than symbolic.

auto-cce16c2524a0.headline: Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro trade sharper jabs in tight Brazil runoff debate
auto-cce16c2524a0.summary:
Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro held a final televised debate on October 23, 2026, ahead of the runoff vote on October 25. The exchanges were less heated than their first debate, though both still traded personal insults over experience, spending and alleged ties to paramilitary groups. Polling showed the two level at 50 percent each. The result could either push Latin America's largest country toward a rightward trend or keep it under the left.

The campaign has also been shaped by court fights over social media, with both sides seeking to disqualify the other and an electoral court demanding explanations from Meta and X on political ad distribution and their use of artificial intelligence.

actors.why: Tight runoff will decide whether Brazil keeps its left-wing government or shifts right.

auto-111571bb1e0b.headline: Taiz residents face mounting water shortages under Houthi siege
auto-111571bb1e0b.summary: Drinking water in Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, has reached crisis levels in recent weeks, according to humanitarian groups. Houthi rebels, who are backed by Iran, have besieged the city in their widening conflict with government forces. Access to wells is limited, desalination plants are short of fuel, and water trucks are largely blocked from entering, leaving the city's more than one million residents with barely enough to get by. Families are rationing every drop, with one mother reporting her household now stretches a 10-litre supply over about four days.

auto-4ee11ef7d5e5.summary: US President Donald Trump has suggested imposing tariffs of 200% on both Ukraine and Russia. Trump then undercut the proposal by saying the United States does not buy enough from either country for such duties to work. The remarks were reported by Ukrainska Pravda, which cited a Clash Report account of his comments.
