Accused of pressuring Starlink limits and strained relations with Kyiv
Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries and Crimea continue to disrupt Moscow

impact_points: Ukraine's military depends on Starlink and Starshield for drone piloting and frontline logistics, so the restriction disrupted operations.
The US faces diplomatic tension with Ukraine and its European allies over sanctions relief and Russian oil imports.

auto-c32bf93441f6.headline: Settlers attempt to enter elderly Palestinian man's West Bank home
auto-c32bf93441f6.summary: Mohammed Al-Obaiyat, a Palestinian who has lived in his home since before Israel occupied the West Bank, reports rising attacks from nearby Israeli settlements around his village of Umm Safa. Armed settlers have tried to break into his house. Israeli forces have also ordered him to vacate the property within a few weeks. The report focuses on the pressure facing one family as settlement activity grows around them.

actors.why: Palestinian family faces armed intrusion attempts and an order to leave their home
Israeli forces issued the eviction order, and settlers involved draw attention to Israel's conduct

impact_points: Palestinian residents of Umm Safa face displacement pressure from settler violence and military orders to leave.
Israel faces scrutiny over settler attacks and enforcement actions against Palestinians in occupied territory.

auto-eae9fbcbe9b7.headline: Missile strike lands near Aden airport after governor leaves
auto-eae9fbcbe9b7.summary:
A ballistic missile struck near Aden International Airport in Yemen shortly after Governor Abdulrahman Sheikh had left the site during an inspection tour. Sheikh, who is also Yemen's minister of state, told Asharq Al-Awsat he was unharmed and that the runway rehabilitation, roughly 70 to 80 percent complete, was funded by a Saudi programme. He said his tour continued and that security agencies had uncovered several Houthi sleeper cells in Aden and other provinces.

Sheikh also described ongoing shortages of cooking gas, electricity and medicines in the city, and credited Saudi and King Salman aid bodies with help on supplies.

actors.why: Missile attack targeted the governor and hit near the airport in Aden
Its development programme funds the runway work and aid supports Aden

impact_points: Yemen's Aden authorities face continued Houthi missile and drone threats while rebuilding infrastructure and services.
Saudi Arabia's reconstruction and aid programmes remain central to Aden's airport repairs and medical supply deliveries.

auto-49706a452187.headline: Rybakina reaches Ningbo final, will face Fernandez seeking back-to-back title
auto-49706a452187.summary: Top seed Elena Rybakina beat Russia's Diana Shnaider 6-3, 7-5 in the semifinal at the Ningbo Open in eastern China, booking a final against Canada's Leylah Fernandez. Fernandez, unseeded, earned her place by defeating Czech player Marie Bouzkova by the same scoreline. Rybakina, the defending champion and reigning Australian and US Open winner, had dropped out of Wuhan with a foot injury and lost in Beijing earlier. The final is set for Sunday.

actors.why: Fernandez reached the final as an unseeded player, a strong result
Hosts the tournament in Ningbo, staging a major international event
Shnaider, a Russian sixth seed, was knocked out in the semifinal
Rybakina, a leading player, is set to contest the final

impact_points: Canada's Leylah Fernandez has a chance to win her first Ningbo title and a major career result.
Elena Rybakina, Kazakhstan-linked world number one, can strengthen her form before the WTA Finals in November.

auto-d6a7c95ae05a.headline: ICC deputy prosecutor says court's work continues despite new US sanctions
auto-d6a7c95ae05a.summary:
Nazhat Shameem Khan, who is co-leading the International Criminal Court's office until a new chief prosecutor is named, told the Guardian that US sanctions are starting to affect some staff, particularly with banking. She said the court has not cut any investigations because of them, and that work on the Gaza war and other cases has advanced, though secret court orders mean little can be disclosed. The sanctions were announced by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who gave the court six months to respond to US concerns.

The court is moving its software away from Microsoft to European alternatives and negotiating with service providers on banking and health insurance. Khan also said the court's former chief prosecutor, Karim Khan, who denies misconduct allegations, was removed in July.

actors.why: Rubio's sanctions target the ICC, which the US administration openly opposes
ICC headquarters host country, where the court's operations and staff are based
Netanyahu faces an ICC war crimes warrant, and Gaza investigations are ongoing

impact_points: The ICC and its staff face banking and everyday access problems under new US sanctions, though its investigations are said to continue.
Israel's Netanyahu and the wider Gaza war file remain in focus, with no new public charges announced since late 2024.

auto-82e58991d0d7.headline: Kyiv says Starlink access restored as strikes continue on both sides
auto-82e58991d0d7.summary: Ukraine's defence minister, Yevhenii Khmara, said restrictions on military use of Starlink and Starshield satellite links have been lifted after more than a week of disruption that hit drone operations. He credited talks with Washington and President Zelenskyy's diplomacy, though it remains unclear who imposed the limits; US President Donald Trump denied responsibility. Separately, negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US are expected to meet in Abu Dhabi in early November. Strikes continued in Ukraine and Russia, with several deaths reported on both sides.

actors.why: Satellite links restored for drones, but attacks and deaths continue across the country
Talks with Kyiv eased the dispute, yet tensions over the Starlink limits and sanctions persist
Ukrainian strikes hit petrochemical and electronics plants, while peace talks are being planned

impact_points: Ukraine regains reliable satellite communications for its military and drone missions, easing a key operational problem.
Ukraine-US ties remain strained, while Russia faces Ukrainian strikes on its plants and expected talks in Abu Dhabi.

auto-e793f738c3d2.headline: Israel seals off Hebron area and begins demolitions after deadly checkpoint attack
auto-e793f738c3d2.summary: Two Israeli soldiers were killed and three wounded at a checkpoint outside Hebron in the occupied West Bank, after two Palestinian gunmen opened fire. Both attackers were shot dead. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the military would destroy the neighbourhood the attackers came from, and Israeli forces have started demolishing Palestinian buildings there. Netanyahu also cordoned off Hebron and the nearby city of Halhul, and said plans for a large West Bank operation had been reviewed, without giving a date. The attack comes days before Israel's general election.

actors.why: Two soldiers killed and a major West Bank operation being prepared
Homes demolished and Hebron and Halhul placed under cordon

impact_points: Palestinian residents of Hebron and the surrounding neighbourhood face demolitions, displacement and movement restrictions.
Israel faces heightened security tensions and political pressure in the run-up to its general election.

auto-0896069ea0af.headline: Melania Trump-brokered local truce set for Russian-held Oleshky
auto-0896069ea0af.summary:
The White House says Melania Trump helped secure a localised ceasefire in Oleshky, a city in Russian-occupied Ukraine where residents are cut off without food, medicine or clean water. Both Russia and Ukraine confirmed the arrangement, which is meant to allow aid deliveries and the evacuation of residents, with fire set to stop from 02:00 GMT on 27 October. The White House did not say how long the truce would last. Only about 6,000 people are thought to remain in the city, which Russia seized in early 2022.

Ukraine's MP Davyd Arakhamia said an operation to open the settlement would follow the ceasefire, while the Kremlin said residents wishing to leave would be allowed to do so.

actors.why: Gains a chance to reach trapped civilians and deliver aid to Oleshky.
Faces criticism over the blockade but agrees to a truce allowing evacuations.
Claims diplomatic credit through Melania Trump's brokering of the truce.

impact_points: Ukraine gains a route to deliver aid and possibly evacuate its citizens from the blockaded city.
Russia faces pressure over a humanitarian crisis it has been criticised for, while allowing evacuations under the truce.

auto-55623195d666.headline: Israeli forces raze Hebron neighbourhood after deadly checkpoint attack
auto-55623195d666.summary: Israeli troops have flattened a large part of the Ein Deir Baha district in Hebron, in the occupied West Bank, after two gunmen attacked a military checkpoint outside the city on Friday. Two Israeli soldiers and both attackers died in the gunfight. Local Palestinian officials say around 1,500 people have been forced from their homes, and the whole city of 250,000 has been cut off by checkpoints. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich vowed a harsh response ahead of Israeli elections in four days. The Israeli army had not yet responded to requests for comment on the demolitions.

actors.why: Hundreds of families displaced and homes razed in collective punishment
Government pursues harsh retaliation, facing criticism ahead of elections

impact_points: Palestinian families in Hebron are losing homes, with local officials estimating around 1,500 people displaced.
Israel faces criticism over collective punishment, while its leaders use the operation in the run-up to elections.

auto-80d0cc63ca5b.headline: Italy deploys troops in Milan ahead of renewed cost-of-living protests
auto-80d0cc63ca5b.summary: Demonstrations were called in eight Italian cities on Saturday, opposing Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government and rising living costs, a week after Milan protests turned into clashes and looting. The loosely organised October 17 Movement has been a leading force behind the actions, alongside students, unions and antiwar groups. Authorities responded with 500 soldiers sent to Milan and a wave of police raids, including dozens of arrests of mostly minors. Protest locations were kept secret until the last moment, and police said they were questioning the group's Instagram administrator.

actors.why: Domestic unrest, troop deployment and mass arrests strain the government's authority.

impact_points: Italy's government faces mounting domestic pressure over living costs, security and public services.
Young protesters, many under 18, face prosecution and possible detention amid debate over social media's role.

auto-ab6fe6a9313d.headline: Jordan boosts security after gunmen kill seven at Karak church
auto-ab6fe6a9313d.summary:
Gunmen opened fire inside a church in Hmoud, in Jordan's Karak governorate, during a funeral on Friday, killing seven people and wounding at least 34. The attackers arrived by car, shot inside the building and fled; no group has claimed responsibility. Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya called the perpetrators a group of extremists and said authorities were pursuing them. King Abdullah II vowed the harshest penalties. The death toll was initially reported differently before officials settled on seven.

Witnesses described panic among the 150 to 200 people inside, and the attack reportedly lasted around 15 minutes. Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun condemned the attack on the church.

actors.why: Lethal attack on a church; security tightened and a manhunt launched
President Aoun condemned the attack as a violation of religious and humanitarian values

impact_points: Jordan's Christian community in Karak faces grief, fear and heightened security after a rare, deadly attack.
Jordan's security forces face pressure to find the attackers and show a tougher stance against militancy.

auto-fc213a687b2d.headline: Drone strike on Nikopol-area village shop leaves four injured, one a teenager
auto-fc213a687b2d.summary: A drone attack hit a food shop in a village within Pokrovske hromada in the Nikopol district of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine, on Saturday, 24 October, after 09:00. Ukraine's National Police said the strike hit a shop where people were present. A 14-year-old boy was seriously hurt and taken to hospital in Dnipro, while three men aged 45 to 58 suffered moderate injuries and are receiving treatment. The building and a metal fence were damaged, and investigators are assessing the full impact.

actors.why: Civilians injured, including a 14-year-old, and property damaged in the strike
Russian forces are reported to have launched the attack drone

impact_points: Ukraine faces civilian casualties, including a child, from a drone strike on a local shop in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast.
Russia is named as the source of the drone attack, which the Ukrainian police attribute to Russian forces.

auto-d88f510fa741.headline: One dead, two hurt in strike on Lozova business in Kharkiv region
auto-d88f510fa741.summary: A man was killed and two civilians, aged 26 and 43, were wounded when a strike hit a business in Lozova, in Ukraine's Kharkiv Oblast, on Saturday 24 October, according to regional police. The two injured people were taken to hospital for treatment. Officers and emergency crews were at the scene, collecting evidence. Investigators opened a criminal case treating the attack as a war crime under Ukraine's Criminal Code, Article 438. The strike was attributed to Russian forces.

actors.why: Civilian killed and two injured in strike, war-crimes case opened
Attributed attack on civilian business draws war-crimes investigation

impact_points: Ukraine suffers another civilian death and injuries, with a criminal war-crimes investigation now opened into the strike.
Russia faces accusations of targeting a commercial site in Kharkiv Oblast, a claim that could fuel further international condemnation.

auto-8216a0f24be0.headline: Paris protest begins at Porte d'Italie after route is changed at last minute
auto-8216a0f24be0.summary: A cost-of-living demonstration got underway in Paris at Porte d'Italie after organisers' route was altered at the last moment. The report says France was bracing for another day of protests nationwide, with extra police deployed to prevent a repeat of the violence seen after last Saturday's demonstrations. In Lyon, where protests were banned, police used tear gas to disperse roughly 150 people. Government figures put last weekend's turnout above half a million, and the movement began with high school student protests over conditions and resources.

actors.why: Nationwide protests and violence strain security and public trust in government

impact_points: France faces renewed street unrest and heavy policing as cost-of-living protests continue across the country.
Paris museums and luxury shops have closed or boarded up after looting, hitting businesses and cultural sites.

auto-451a6aeadadb.headline: Houthi attacks on Aden and Saudi strikes in Yemen leave casualties on both sides
auto-451a6aeadadb.summary:
Yemen's Houthi movement said it struck a naval base and a military camp in Aden, the southern city serving as the interim seat of the internationally recognised government, and accused Riyadh of killing 16 people in strikes on Aden, Sanaa and a Red Sea port. Houthi media reported further deaths from Saudi airstrikes in Sanaa and Hodeida. A Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two ballistic missiles aimed at the Saudi cities of Taif and Yanbu, and the fighting between the two sides was continuing. The Houthi claims could not be independently verified.

The article also covers a deadly attack on a church in Karak, southern Jordan, where the death toll reached nine, and Israeli forces displacing about 1,200 Palestinians from Hebron in the occupied West Bank.

actors.why: Targeted by Houthi missiles toward Taif and Yanbu; coalition strikes ongoing
Civilians killed in airstrikes across Sanaa, Hodeida and Aden
Houthis, Iran-aligned, press attacks on Saudi Arabia
Deadly church attack in Karak; king ordered firm security response
Israeli forces displaced around 1,200 residents of Hebron

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces renewed missile fire and cross-border strikes as its war with the Houthis escalates.
Yemen's civilians in Aden, Sanaa and Hodeida face deaths and displacement from the intensified airstrikes and attacks.

auto-bca30aad693e.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts two Houthi missiles aimed at western Saudi cities
auto-bca30aad693e.summary: A Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen's Houthi movement said it shot down two ballistic missiles that the group launched toward Taif and Yanbu on Saturday. The strikes came as fighting between the two sides continued. Saudi civil defence briefly sent alerts for Taif, Yanbu, Mecca and Jeddah, then cancelled them about ten minutes later once the threat had passed.

actors.why: Missiles aimed at its cities were intercepted, but the threat to civilians persists
Houthi forces launched the missiles as their fighting with Saudi-led coalition continues
Iran-aligned Houthis are firing on Saudi territory, linking Tehran to the escalation

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces renewed missile threats reaching deep into its western cities, including the holy city of Mecca.
Iran-aligned Houthis continue an active confrontation with Saudi forces, keeping regional tensions and security risks elevated.

auto-231d8cdae06d.headline: Starlink speeds restored for Ukraine after week-long military disruption
auto-231d8cdae06d.summary:
Ukraine's Defense Ministry said Starlink and its military counterpart Starshield are again running at high speeds, following more than a week of restrictions that disrupted frontline operations. The limits, which began around October 14, reportedly stopped Ukrainian units from intercepting Russian attack drones and forced some drone missions to be cancelled. The ministry did not say whether service had been fully restored, and the system's maximum speeds are not publicly disclosed.

The disruption came as tensions rose between Washington and Kyiv over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries, and after a US deal to buy Russian diesel. Responsibility is disputed: some reports blame the White House, others say SpaceX chief Elon Musk ordered the slowdown, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the decisions were commercial. Congress has called for an investigation.

actors.why: Drone interception and operations were disrupted; service now reported restored
Tensions with Kyiv and a congressional probe over who ordered restrictions
Russian drone attacks were harder to intercept while Ukrainian links were limited

impact_points: Ukraine's military lost reliable satellite links for drone interception and frontline communications during the restrictions.
SpaceX and US lawmakers face scrutiny over who controlled the service and whether it was used for political leverage.

auto-286eac363129.headline: Smoke rises over Oryol after reported strike on Russian plant
auto-286eac363129.summary: Video posted online on 23 October shows smoke rising above the Russian city of Oryol following a reported attack on a factory there. The regional governor said three people died in the strike, and emergency services said five more were seriously injured and being treated in intensive care. Satellite imagery was used to confirm the footage was filmed in Oryol, but the exact date and conditions of the recording could not be established.

actors.why: Deadly strike on a factory in Oryol, with three killed and five seriously wounded
Reported to be the source of the attack on the Russian factory

impact_points: Russia faces a deadly attack on an industrial site inside its territory, with several people killed and injured.
Local residents of Oryol and the factory's workforce bear the immediate human and safety consequences of the strike.

auto-b0b8edf25b89.headline: Russia reports drone attack on Togliatti sites; Ukraine claims hit on petrochemical plant
auto-b0b8edf25b89.summary: Russian officials said a drone attack damaged facilities in the city of Togliatti, while Ukraine said a petrochemical plant there was struck. The article notes these competing accounts and that the claims could not be independently confirmed in the material available. The report centres on the contrasting descriptions of which sites were hit and how much damage resulted, with the Togliatti location at the heart of the dispute.

actors.why: Reported drone attack damaged facilities on Russian soil, a clear setback
Claims a strike on a petrochemical plant, a gain in pressure on Russia

impact_points: Russia faces reported damage to industrial facilities in Togliatti, with officials attributing the attack to drones.
Ukraine is claiming credit for striking a petrochemical plant, a claim the report says is disputed.

auto-6bc17e4856c3.headline: Melania Trump-brokered truce to open Oleshky for aid and evacuation
auto-6bc17e4856c3.summary: The White House says Melania Trump helped secure a localised ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, due to start on 29 October. Russia and Ukraine have both confirmed the arrangement, which aims to allow aid deliveries and evacuations for residents who are cut off and short of food, medicine and clean water. Both sides said their forces would stop firing from 01:00 GMT on 27 October. The truce's duration was not specified, and residents may evacuate toward either Russia or Ukraine.

actors.why: Gains a path to aid and evacuation for Oleshky residents after a long blockade.
Faces pressure over the city's crisis but secures a localised truce it helped agree.
Melania Trump's personal diplomacy claims a humanitarian success on the Russia-Ukraine file.

impact_points: Ukraine and its residents in Oleshky could gain aid access and evacuation routes, though Kyiv says the area has long been under blockade.
Russia gains a humanitarian gesture after the Kremlin acknowledged a critical supply crisis in the city it controls.

auto-eb3b916782fc.headline: Reported Ukrainian drone strikes hit Omsk petrochemical plant and warehouse in Siberia
auto-eb3b916782fc.summary: Monitoring channels reported that Ukraine struck several targets in Omsk, a Russian city roughly 2,500 kilometres from the Ukrainian border, on October 24. A fire was said to have broken out at the Omsky Kauchuk petrochemical plant, a major Russian producer of synthetic rubber and a fuel additive, and an Ozon warehouse was reportedly hit too. Omsk's regional governor confirmed a drone attack on a logistics hub and said staff were evacuated. The Kyiv Independent could not immediately verify these reports.

actors.why: Reported drone strikes damage a petrochemical plant and logistics hub deep inside Russia
Reported strikes target military-linked industry, aiming to reduce Russia's military-economic potential

impact_points: Russia is affected as its petrochemical and logistics capacity in Omsk reportedly suffers damage and disruption.
Ozon and the wider Russian e-commerce sector face disruption, given the company's role in the national economy.

auto-b63532f2ede4.headline: Houthis report five family members killed in Saudi strike on Hodeidah home
auto-b63532f2ede4.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement said a Saudi air strike hit a house in the Al-Tuhayta district of Hodeidah, killing five members of one family and wounding a daughter. The claim was relayed by the group's Al-Masirah television channel. The report comes as both sides in the Hodeidah fighting continue to carry out strikes, and the casualty figures are the Houthis' account, which could not be independently verified in this report.

actors.why: Accused of a strike that killed civilians; faces criticism over the attack
Civilian family killed in Hodeidah fighting; the wider conflict continues

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces accusations over civilian deaths in Hodeidah, which could increase international scrutiny of its air campaign.
Yemeni civilians in Hodeidah are exposed to deadly strikes as fighting between the Houthis and their opponents continues.

auto-891b25b7c12a.headline: Ukrainian drone strike on Oryol plant leaves three dead, Russian governor reports
auto-891b25b7c12a.summary: Russia's governor of the Oryol region said a Ukrainian strike on an industrial enterprise in the area killed three people. The attack is the central event described in the report, and the governor's account is the source for the death toll, which was not independently confirmed in the material available here. Reuters reported the incident under a Russia dateline.

actors.why: Three killed at an Oryol enterprise, a clear domestic cost from the strike
Credited by Russian officials with a strike that caused deaths

impact_points: Russia faces a fresh loss of life and disruption at an industrial site in Oryol.
Ukraine is implicated as the attacker, which keeps the two sides' hostilities active.

auto-9a889f52f2b4.headline: Oil nears five-month high as Hormuz tanker attacks and stalled talks grow
auto-9a889f52f2b4.summary:
Oil prices rose toward their highest level in five months as attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz increased and efforts to end the US-Israel war on Iran stalled. Brent crude climbed above $110 a barrel on Wednesday. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they struck several tankers, which Washington disputed. The Houthis have also seized territory in Yemen near the Bab al-Mandeb chokepoint, while the world's emergency oil stocks have fallen to their lowest levels in decades.

Analysts warn that usable reserves outside China are limited, with Japan holding nearly half of what remains. A full closure of Hormuz and Houthi blockades could cut Middle Eastern crude supply sharply.

actors.why: Iran's forces are attacking tankers and talks remain deadlocked
Faces disputed tanker attacks and a stalled effort to end the war
Its oil exports rely on Red Sea routes threatened by Houthi blockade
Holds nearly half of remaining usable global emergency oil stocks
Houthis seized territory near Bab al-Mandeb strait

impact_points: Importing countries such as Japan, Europe and India face shrinking emergency oil reserves and higher prices.
Gulf oil producers, especially Saudi Arabia, risk export losses if Hormuz closes and Red Sea routes are blocked.

auto-8b102ec44cd3.headline: Ukrainian drone strike on Russian Oryol plant leaves three dead, governor reports
auto-8b102ec44cd3.summary: Russia's governor of the Oryol region said a Ukrainian strike on an industrial enterprise there killed three people. The attack targeted a facility in the Russian city of Oryol, which lies inside Russia rather than in Ukraine. The governor's account is the source of the casualty figure, and it could not be independently verified from the material available here. The report sits within the wider war, in which Kyiv and Moscow continue to exchange long-range strikes.

actors.why: Three killed in Ukrainian strike on Oryol enterprise, per governor
Strike launched by Ukraine; exposure to retaliation and scrutiny

impact_points: Russia is affected by a deadly strike on an industrial site in Oryol, with three people killed.
Ukraine faces continued pressure from cross-border strikes as the war grinds on, with peace efforts uncertain.
